sections.title: Start here: an investor built around power
sections.read: Four kinds of money sit under one name, and none of them signs an equipment order itself.
ps: **The manager.** KKR & Co. Inc. invests other people's money in private equity, infrastructure, real estate and credit, and earns fees and a share of profits.
**The insurer.** Global Atlantic, which KKR owns outright, invests policyholders' premiums for decades, much of it in long-lived assets.

**The vehicles.** Closed-end funds, an open-ended core fund, a USD 50bn partnership with Energy Capital Partners, and Helix Digital Infrastructure, a company built to own data centres and the power behind them.
**The platforms.** STTGDC, CyrusOne, ContourGlobal, Avantus and others employ the engineers who buy equipment. This guide teaches how each layer works and which platforms actually place orders.

sections.title: Why an insurer's money suits infrastructure
ps: An {{annuity}} is a contract in which a saver pays now and the insurer guarantees payments or a return later. The insurer invests the premiums in its {{general account}} and earns the spread between what those investments yield and what it promised.

A promise due in twenty years is best matched by an asset that pays for twenty years: a transmission line on a regulated return, a data centre on a long lease, a solar farm on a long contract. That is why Global Atlantic's accounts bought 50% stakes in operating renewables portfolios and help fund KKR's partnership with Energy Capital Partners.

The weakness is leverage and liquidity. If investments disappoint, the promises remain, and trade press has criticised insurer-backed managers on exactly that point. Insurance money buys finished, income-producing assets; it finances equipment buyers rather than buying equipment itself.

sections.title: Co-owning a landlord fifty-fifty
sections.read: Equal owners protect each other — and slow each other down.
ps: KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners, now part of BlackRock, took CyrusOne private in March 2022 for about USD 15bn including debt. The European Commission cleared it as {{joint control}}; the split is widely reported as 50:50 but is stated in no first-party document read for the dossier.

Under {{co-control}}, a shareholders' agreement lists reserved matters — budgets, large contracts, new debt, a sale — that need both owners' consent. Neither sponsor can impose a strategy alone, which protects each from the other but means a large equipment frame may need two investment committees.
Co-owners must also agree on an exit. Reuters reported in August 2026 that they are preparing an {{IPO}} as early as 2027, a route that lets both sell down gradually.

sections.title: Owning 19.9% of wires you will never run
sections.read: A regulated return is predictable enough that an investor accepts no control.
ps: KKR and PSP Investments, 50/50 partners, paid USD 2.82bn in June 2025 for 19.9% of AEP's Ohio and Indiana Michigan {{transmission company}} subsidiaries. AEP keeps control and 'will continue to operate and maintain these transmission facilities'.

A transmission company earns a return on its {{rate base}} — the depreciated value of its lines and substations — through a {{FERC formula rate}}. The more it invests, the more it earns, and the formula makes that income predictable.

The utility gets equity for a large capital plan without issuing as many new shares; the investors get steady income without operating risk. The transformers and breakers the transmission companies buy are still AEP's choices: KKR's money pays for them without deciding them.

sections.title: Helix: a data-centre company that buys power from its investor
sections.read: The most unusual structure in this corpus's capital segment, and a caution for outside suppliers.
ps: KKR launched Helix Digital Infrastructure on 11 June 2026 with more than USD 10bn of commitments to build hyperscale data centres together with generation, transmission and fibre. NVIDIA, the Kuwait Investment Authority and Vistra are among its founding investors.

**The loop.** Vistra committed up to USD 1.0bn: half up front, half once Helix meets milestones for buying power from Vistra's existing plants, or at Vistra's choice. Vistra is Helix's {{preferred power partner}}, so part of the investment is tied to Helix becoming Vistra's customer.

**The first look.** KKR's release says founding investors 'may have certain rights, such as priority or first look rights, to provide goods or services to Helix investments'. A {{first-look right}} lets an investor see a supply opportunity before anyone else.

**Why power is inside.** KKR's research argues that 'the ultimate limiting factor for building data centers isn't capital; it's power'. A vehicle that owns generation beside its data centres controls the scarce input. No Helix project or supplier had been named by 26 September 2026.

sections.title: Buying a platform abroad — and the DC-power testbed that came with it
sections.read: The one KKR platform with a high-voltage DC programme on the record.
ps: KKR and Singtel agreed in February 2026 to buy the roughly 82% of STT GDC they did not already own for S$6.6bn in cash, at about S$13.8bn of {{enterprise value}}; the deal completed on 2 September 2026 with KKR at 75% and Singtel at 25%. Half the price is {{deferred consideration}}, due on the first anniversary or on an earlier change of control.

Enterprise value prices the whole company including debt; the cash price buys only the equity not already held. Keeping a local strategic partner gives a foreign investor a domestic ally in a country that treats data centres as critical infrastructure.

In January 2026 STT GDC launched a live {{HVDC}} testbed for AI racks, built with LITEON and supported by the start-up Amperesand, and said it 'plans to deploy this technology in future data centres in Singapore'. Amperesand makes a {{solid-state transformer}}, which converts medium-voltage AC to DC electronically. STTGDC's engineering team is therefore the nearest thing to an SST buyer anywhere in KKR's portfolio.

sections.title: Exits: how a fund makes its return
sections.read: A fund earns when it sells, and the best buyer is often a company in the same business.
ps: KKR's impact fund bought CoolIT, a liquid-cooling maker, in 2023 and sold it to Ecolab for about USD 4.75bn in cash, closing on 2 July 2026 — about 15 times its cost per KKR. A **strategic buyer** in a related business can pay more than another fund because it can combine the target with what it already sells.

KKR and other shareholders agreed on 31 August 2026 to sell USI, an insurance broker, to Aon for USD 17.0bn, with closing expected in the fourth quarter. Proceeds flow back to fund investors and to KKR's own balance sheet, and feed the next commitments.

Signed is not closed. USI, EDF power solutions North America and the Sempra Infrastructure Partners stake were all signed but not closed on 26 September 2026, and a dossier records each as announced until closing is confirmed.

sections.title: Flashcards
sections.read: Concept recall — none of these asks for a date, a name or a fund size.

cards.q: Why does an {{annuity}} writer want infrastructure in its {{general account}}?
cards.a: Its promises run for decades, so it needs long-lived assets with steady income, such as regulated transmission or long-leased data centres.

cards.q: What is the difference between a {{closed-end fund}} and an {{open-ended fund}}?
cards.a: A closed-end fund raises once and returns the money after about ten years, so it must sell; an open-ended fund has no end date and can hold assets indefinitely.

cards.q: What can each owner do under {{co-control}} that a minority holder cannot?
cards.a: Veto the reserved matters — major budgets, contracts, debt and a sale.

cards.q: Why would a utility sell 19.9% of a {{transmission company}}?
cards.a: To raise equity for its capital plan without issuing as many new shares, while keeping control and operation of the lines.

cards.q: What does a {{first-look right}} give a founding investor in a project company?
cards.a: The chance to see, and match or take, an opportunity to supply goods or services before an outside supplier.

cards.q: Why does DC distribution with a {{solid-state transformer}} save power?
cards.a: It removes conversion stages between the grid and the chips, and each conversion loses a few per cent as heat.

cards.q: A battery is sold as 200 MW / 800 MWh. What is its duration?
cards.a: Four hours: energy (MWh) divided by power (MW).

cards.q: Why can {{enterprise value}} be much larger than the cash paid for a stake?
cards.a: Enterprise value prices the whole company including its debt; the cash buys only the equity being purchased.

items.q: KKR holds 19.9% of a transmission company that is buying 50 large transformers. Who chooses the supplier?
c: The utility that operates the company
items.why: The majority owner keeps control and operation; the minority investor funds without deciding.

items.q: Why did KKR create a separate vehicle for AI data centres?
c: Its diversified funds limit how much can go into one theme
Its insurer could not invest in data centres
items.why: KKR's CFO said the infrastructure funds 'carry diversification guidelines that limit how much we could dedicate to a single theme'.

items.q: Which KKR platform has a high-voltage DC programme on the record?
items.why: STT GDC's January 2026 testbed with LITEON and Amperesand, which it plans to deploy in future Singapore data centres.

items.q: 526 containers of 5.64 MWh each, discharging over four hours, deliver about how much power?
A signed acquisition awaits federal energy approval. How should a dossier record the buyer's relationship to the target?
items.why: Signing binds the parties to conditions; ownership passes only at closing.

items.q: Why can a strategic buyer outbid a fund for a company?
c: It can combine the target with its existing business and cut shared costs
It is not subject to antitrust review
items.why: Synergies make the target worth more to a buyer already in a related business.

glossary.d: A contractual right to see an opportunity — here, to supply goods or services to a project — before outside parties, with the chance to match or take it.

In Helix Digital Infrastructure, the founding investor (Vistra) designated to supply power to the vehicle's projects on a preferred basis; Vistra called it 'a preferred power partner, not a requirement'.
Decisions a shareholders' agreement says need every co-owner's consent — typically budgets, large contracts, new debt and a sale.
A company in the same or a related business, which can pay more for a target than a financial investor because it can combine operations and cut shared costs.
